newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on weak U.S. dollar overseas.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on weak U.S. dollar overseas.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday for a fifth consecutive daily gain, once again reflecting the U.S. dollar's relative weakness overseas, dealers said.
The local dollar ended at T$27.507, off a T$27.492 high, against Tuesday's T$27.523 close.
Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$301.5 million.
Dealers attributed the rise in part to tight liquidity in a domestic money market where investors had been forced to sell U.S. dollars in exchange for Taiwan dollars.
"Liquidity tightened further today after the government's sudden decision to declare that Friday and Saturday will be state holidays," said one dealer.

Dealers said the additional two days of holiday on the heels of February's weeklong Chinese lunar new year shutdown will make enterprises' and banks' fund operations more difficult and further tighten liquidity.
The government on Tuesday announced that February 28 would be a state holiday to commemorate a 1947 massacre, with markets closed on Friday and Saturday.
But dealers noted active U.S. dollar buying from importers.
"After all, the Taiwan dollar has risen for five straight days. Therefore, importers began showing keen interest to buy U.S. dollars when the Taiwan dollar rose above T$27.50," the dealer said.
Dealers said the Taiwan dollar should consolidate around current levels in coming sessions.
A T$27.48-27.53 range was seen for Thursday.
